questions.q: What does a Navigation object do?
options: It's a dedicated dashboard object whose button switches the viewer to a different dashboard or story when clicked
It automatically filters every sheet on the dashboard
It resizes the dashboard to fit any device
It permanently merges two dashboards into one
questions.explain: A Navigation object lives in the Objects panel and its whole purpose is providing a clickable button that switches the viewer to a different dashboard or story.

questions.q: How is a Go to Sheet action different from a Navigation object?
options: A Go to Sheet action triggers navigation from an interaction with a mark (via the Actions dialog); a Navigation object requires a dedicated button
A Go to Sheet action can only be used on Tableau Server, never Desktop
They are identical in every respect
A Go to Sheet action can only target the same dashboard it's configured on
questions.explain: A Navigation object needs its own button in the Objects panel. A Go to Sheet action, configured through the Actions dialog like filter/highlight/URL/parameter/set actions, triggers navigation from clicking, hovering, or selecting from a menu on a mark instead.

questions.q: What does a Show/Hide button do, and what kind of object does it apply to?
options: It adds a toggle (usually an X icon) that shows or hides a floating object without disturbing the tiled layout underneath
It permanently deletes the object it's attached to
It only works on tiled objects, never floating ones
It converts a floating object into a Navigation object
questions.explain: Show/Hide buttons are specifically for floating objects — they let a viewer toggle visibility on demand, which is exactly what makes Lesson 80's floating layout mode practically useful (e.g. a filter panel that tucks away).

questions.q: How do you make a dashboard title dynamic (e.g. showing the currently selected region)?
options: Edit Title, then use the Insert menu to add placeholders like <Sheet Name> or a field/parameter value
Dynamic titles require a custom Python script outside Tableau
Titles in Tableau can never include field or parameter values — only static text
You must rebuild the dashboard from scratch for each possible title value
questions.explain: The Edit Title dialog's Insert menu lets you drop in dynamic placeholders — <Sheet Name>, field values, or parameter values — so the title text updates as selections or parameters change.

questions.q: Why does this lesson pair a dynamic title with a parameter action from Lesson 83 as a practical example?
options: Because clicking a mark to set a parameter, combined with a title that displays that parameter's value, confirms to the viewer exactly what they're now looking at
Because parameter actions are required before any title can be edited at all
Because dynamic titles only work when no parameter exists
Because this combination disables all other dashboard actions
questions.explain: A parameter action lets a click set a parameter's value; a dynamic title referencing that parameter shows the viewer what they selected without them having to check a filter panel separately — a small combination that makes a dashboard feel more responsive.
